name: Floodlight OpenFlow Controller
what_it_is: Floodlight is an open-source, Java-based OpenFlow SDN controller that manages network forwarding behavior via a modular architecture with a REST API and web UI. It supports OpenFlow versions 1.0 through 1.5 and is designed to control physical and virtual switches, routers, and access points.
components: LinkDiscoveryManager (LLDP-based link discovery with latency measurement)
DeviceManagerImpl (host/device tracking by MAC, IP, VLAN, switch port)
StatisticsCollector (periodic port and flow stats polling)
RestApiServer (embedded Restlet-based HTTP/HTTPS REST server on port 8080/8081)
measurement: StatisticsCollector: periodic port-stats polling (default interval 10 s, configurable)
StatisticsCollector: per-port bandwidth (tx/rx bytes, packets, errors) via SwitchPortBandwidth
StatisticsCollector: flow-rule hit/byte counts via FlowRuleStats
PktInProcessingTime: packet-in processing latency per module
LinkDiscoveryManager: per-link latency history (configurable history size and update threshold)
ControllerMemoryResource: JVM heap usage via REST
configuration: Module list defined in .properties file (floodlightdefault.properties, learningswitch.properties, etc.)
OFSwitchManager.useSsl: YES/NO with keyStorePath and keyStorePassword
Forwarding.match: match fields for reactive flows (in-port, vlan, mac, ip, transport, flag)
Forwarding.idle-timeout: flow idle timeout in seconds (default 5)
SyncManager cluster nodes: JSON array with nodeId, domainId, hostname, port
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection framework; Mininet integration (example/mininet) enables topology-level link failures and host disconnects
JythonDebugInterface: live Python REPL allows manual module manipulation, flow deletion, and state corruption for testing
Static flow entries can be inserted/deleted via REST to simulate routing failures
Controller role can be toggled ACTIVE/STANDBY via REST (ControllerRoleResource) to test HA failover
OFSwitchManager.switchesInitialState allows forcing per-DPID roles at startup to simulate split-brain scenarios
modes: STANDBY (hot-standby for HA, role switchable via REST)
Learning switch mode (learningswitch.properties, reactive L2 forwarding only)
Default multi-module mode (forwarding + firewall + LB + DHCP + ACL)
Benchmarking mode (floodlightbenchmarking.properties, minimal module set for throughput testing)
constraints: No docker-compose file in the repository; deployment requires manual JVM setup or the pre-built Vagrant VM
StatisticsCollector is disabled by default (enable=FALSE); must be explicitly enabled for metrics collection
MemoryStorageSource provides no persistence; all state is lost on restart unless SyncManager persistence is enabled
SyncManager persistence is disabled by default (persistenceEnabled=FALSE)
OFSwitchManager TLS/SSL is disabled by default (useSsl=NO); plaintext OpenFlow is the out-of-the-box mode
Sub-agents cannot be spawned; HA requires external SyncManager cluster configuration with pre-shared keystore
LinkDiscoveryManager relies on LLDP; switches that strip or block LLDP will not appear in the topology graph
The project has not had active upstream commits since ~2020; OpenFlow 1.5 support may be incomplete for newer switch features
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml or Dockerfile in the repository
No built-in packet capture or pcap export capability
No built-in time-series metrics export (no Prometheus/InfluxDB integration)
No GUI-based topology editor (read-only web UI only)
No built-in intent-based northbound API (unlike ONOS or OpenDaylight)
